newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: RTRS-Argentina plans assault on world wheat market.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Argentina plans assault on world wheat market.

text.p: Needing to ship a bumper wheat crop before summer grains arrive to clog up ports, Argentine exporters will be aiming to storm world wheat markets during their harvest rush, grain analysts said.

"Argentina is going to try for around 30 percent of the world market over the three harvest months," said a private analyst, who declined to be named. He said the country normally supplied about 22 percent of world wheat exports in its December to February peak period.

"We have to rush out about five million tonnes and we have about three months to do that," the analyst said. He was not including estimated sales of another five million-odd tonnes to Argentina's traditional market, Brazil.

While other big exporters like Australia, Canada, the United States and Europe tend to pace their sales, Argentine suppliers traditionally pour what wheat they have into world wheat markets Argentina is the only big wheat exporter not to be a full-fledged member of the rich world.
Its farmers tend to need cash quickly and find credit for the maize, sunflower and soybean harvests which follow wheat hard to come by.

Their crop is prospering in the fields and heading for output which some think could be as much as 15.5 million tonnes. The more conservative say they are betting on only 14 million tonnes, but either way production will soar from 1995/96's nine million tonnes and exports could double to 10 million tonnes.
Harvesting is now beginning in the northern reaches of the wheat belt, but will hit top speed in December.

One trader said that forward export sales of 1996/97 wheat had so far reached 3.6 million tonnes, with 900,000 tonnes taken by Brazilian buyers. He said recent sales included 25,000 tonnes to Peru and a 100,000-tonne placement with Bulgaria for December to May shipment, made at the end of last week.

But he said that Brazil will as ever be Argentina's main client: "Okay, they've got a harvest of three million tonnes of wheat, but only two million tonnes are good for bread, so they need to import six million tonnes. Why buy American hard red at $170 when they can buy Argentine at $130?"
Argentine wheat was offered Monday at $130 FOB, or without freight costs, for January to February shipment.
The Brazilians are buying slowly, partly out of a habit of not purchasing far in advance and partly because of the groggy financial state of their milling industry.

Brazil took almost all Argentina's exports last season, but this year the Argentines are having to move further afield. With a home market unhindered by government control, they have been aggresively undercutting European Union producers in what they regard as their home patch in North Africa and the Middle East.
Argentine traders were gleefully contemplating further raids into European territory.
"Turkey is tendering for 100,000 tonnes November 15," one trader said, "But you never know with the Turks, if they like the price they could go and buy 500,000 tonnes."
He said he knew of sales to former Soviet republics, and said there had been requests for prices from Russia.
The analyst said "We are recapturing some traditional markets like Indonesia, and in Southern Africa, but also going where never before like Jordan and Algeria."
While the Europeans have reacted to cheap Argentine wheat by raising their subsidies, the trader said he thought the real competition was elsewhere.

"I think our big competition are Australia and Canada. The Canadians and Australians still have yet to sell much. I think they are betting we will finish placing our crop quickly and leave them time to sell before the new crop American wheat comes along. They might be betting right.
